pairs: Dei et Domini nostri Jesu Christi servus,
and of our Lord Jesus Christ,
to the twelve tribes of the dispersion,
My brothers, when you have fallen into various trials,
scientes quod probatio fidei vestræ patientiam operatur.
knowing that the proving of your faith exercises patience,
and patience brings a work to perfection,
so that you may be perfect and whole,
Si quis autem vestrum indiget sapientia,
But if anyone among you is in need of wisdom,
who gives abundantly to all without reproach,
et non improperat: et dabitur ei.
and it shall be given to him.
Postulet autem in fide nihil hæsitans:
But he should ask with faith,
For he who doubts is like a wave on the ocean,
qui a vento movetur et circumfertur:
which is moved about by the wind and carried away;
non ergo æstimet homo ille quod accipiat aliquid a Domino.
then a man should not consider that he would receive anything from the Lord.
Vir duplex animo inconstans est in omnibus viis suis.
For a man who is of two minds is inconstant in all his ways.
Glorietur autem frater humilis in exaltatione sua:
Now a humble brother should glory in his exaltation,
and a rich one, in his humiliation,
for he will pass away like the flower of the grass.
exortus est enim sol cum ardore,
For the sun has risen with a scorching heat,
and its flower has fallen off,
and the appearance of its beauty has perished.
So also will the rich one wither away,
et dives in itineribus suis marcescet.
Blessed is the man who suffers temptation.
For when he has been proven,
accipiet coronam vitæ, quam repromisit Deus diligentibus se.
he shall receive the crown of life which God has promised to those who love him.
when he is tempted, that he was tempted by God.
For God does not entice toward evils,
and he himself tempts no one.
Unusquisque vero tentatur a concupiscentia sua abstractus, et illectus.
Yet truly, each one is tempted by his own desires, having been enticed and drawn away.
Yet truly sin, when it has been consummated,
And so, do not choose to go astray,
et omne donum perfectum desursum est,
and every perfect gift is from above,
descending from the Father of lights,
with whom there is no change,
Voluntarie enim genuit nos verbo veritatis,
For by his own will he produced us through the Word of truth,
ut simus initium aliquod creaturæ ejus.
so that we might be a kind of beginning among his creatures.
Sit autem omnis homo velox ad audiendum:
So let every man be quick to listen,
Ira enim viri justitiam Dei non operatur.
For the anger of man does not accomplish the justice of God.
having cast away all uncleanness and an abundance of malice,
receive with meekness the newly-grafted Word,
which is able to save your souls.
So be doers of the Word,
Quia si quis auditor est verbi,
For if anyone is a listener of the Word,
hic comparabitur viro consideranti vultum nativitatis suæ in speculo:
he is comparable to a man gazing into a mirror upon the face that he was born with;
et statim oblitus est qualis fuerit.
and promptly forgot what he had seen.
Qui autem perspexerit in legem perfectam libertatis,
But he who gazes upon the perfect law of liberty,
but instead a doer of the work.
hic beatus in facto suo erit.
He shall be blessed in what he does.
Si quis autem putat se religiosum esse,
But if anyone considers himself to be religious,
but he does not restrain his tongue,
but instead seduces his own heart:
such a one’s religion is vanity.
Religio munda et immaculata apud Deum et Patrem, hæc est:
This is religion, clean and undefiled before God the Father:
visitare pupillos et viduas in tribulatione eorum,
to visit orphans and widows in their tribulations,
et immaculatum se custodire ab hoc sæculo.
and to keep yourself immaculate, apart from this age.
